chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: The Vendome in Buffalo: tips, entertainers and playing in odd keys
summary: Luke Stewart held a steady four-piece job at the Vendome for $35 a week, with the dancer sharing tips and customers requesting songs in difficult keys.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, they'd stayed around. They hung around. And oh, Al Gibson, another one, he hung around. He stayed there. Oh, quite a few of them. So we got back, we got back to see them all and they was doing pretty good. Luke was at the -- had a regular job now, a steady job, in the Vendome, you know. He was working there for tips, then he went in and they gave him a job. So they had four pieces. They were working with a piano, bass, drum and guitar. And the entertainers was
You know, and they would give her money, you know.
And she'd go around and she'd come back, and after she went around to all the tables, and she'd dance some more, you know, and go out.
Yeah, that's right. Would she split that?
And she'd split the tips with the band, you know.
And on top of that, the guy's paying $35.00 a week.
And the guys are getting to blow, back of her.

Yeah, and the guys are blowing, and these chicks would come in with different keys. 'I want so and so in B-Natural.' And, 'I want In Dreams I Kiss Your Hand, Madam, in F-Sharp, you know.' So that taught you to play in them keys, you know.

And if you had a good piano man. Because I used to tell them, oh, what's the difference between F-Sharp and a G. But I'd play it right the way she wanted it. So that made you learn your keys, you know. It was good for you there.
